subsystem.name: GenericRuntimeObjects
subsystem.responsibility: Generic runtime object support layer: counted-loop iteration helpers, vehicle physics-body state, fixed-stride element/proximity processing, large UI control-window construction with per-sub-control blocks, reusable linked-node initializers, and session/scoring struct reset.

source_proposals.summary: Reconstructs the generic runtime object layer from twelve validated functions. One DERIVED UI control-window constructor (0x004A70E0) builds a window with ~200 per-sub-control blocks via a uniform block-initializer pattern (GUESS interface ISubControlBlockInitializer). Four GUESS classes cover vehicle physics-body state (0x0045A8E0), fixed-stride element/proximity processing (0x004047D0), a reusable three-field linked node (0x004BAC20), and a session/scoring reset struct (0x004BB950). Seven functions (counted-loop helper 0x00401000, guarded mutex trigger 0x00406640, three getters/accessors, a flag dispatch wrapper, and a null subroutine) have UNKNOWN owners and are kept unowned. No state machine evidence was found. Field semantics and several owner identities remain unresolved; the bulk sub-control-block field offsets are preserved in UIControlWindow's evidence without forcing per-block meaning.

function_roles.role: Generic counted-loop iteration helper: invokes a caller-supplied __thiscall callback a4 over a3 elements, advancing the element pointer by stride a2 each iteration; returns the last callback result (or a3-1 when count is zero).

Counted element-loop driver: reads element count from this+0x130, loops calling VehicleProximity (0x004FB2E0) per element of the +0x134 table with a 316-byte stride; invoked from heightfield collision processing (0x00404250).

Guarded mutex trigger: compares this+0xC with argument a2; on match acquires a mutex via MutexLockWithTimeout(1) and returns the lock result, otherwise returns the field value unchanged (not a pure getter).
Trivial read-only getter returning the DWORD at this+0x4.
Trivial read-only getter returning the DWORD at this+0x54.

Vehicle physics body update: writes requested speed limit to +0x24, clamps against +0x1C/+0x20 bounds, runs the velocity/angular-velocity integrator (0x00459AE0) at step 0.0125 when +0xD0 is enabled, computes attitude angles, emits 3D position via 0x0054B4D0, and handles out-of-range/reset paths.
Double-indirected byte accessor: loads the object pointer stored at this+0x0 and returns the BYTE at obj+0x20.
Byte-offset flag dispatch: forms &this[a2] and forwards it to BitFlagSetter (0x004649F0) to set a single bit; used by the entity visibility grid manager.

Constructor of a large UI control window: zeroes the leading callback/state dwords and byte flag, seeds ~200 sub-control blocks with sentinel defaults, vtable pointers from the fixed table 0x005ACB6C..0x005ACBFC, state dword 0 and target/sentinel -1, zeroes tail flags, then applies player-options defaults (0x004AA270).
Reusable three-field node initializer: stores a2 at this+0x0 (data), nulls this+0x4 (next), stores byte flag a3 at this+0x8; used across directory, collision, physics, AI, and network callers.

Session/scoring struct reset: frees owned allocations +0x8C/+0x90/+0x94, counts '1' entries of the +0x94 array into +0x98 before freeing, reinitializes ~40 scalar fields with -1.0/0/-1 defaults, memsets the trailing 0x28-byte block to 0xFF, and returns -1.
Null subroutine: body has no executable statements and returns immediately (IDA nullsub_134 marker; the MK_FP retaddr expression is a decompiler artifact of a bare ret).

class_proposals.name: UIControlWindow
class_proposals.responsibility: Large UI control window object: leading callback/state dwords, a ~200-element array of per-sub-control blocks (each holding a vtable header, a state dword reset to 0, and a target/sentinel dword set to -1), tail flags, and player-options defaults; constructed by 0x004A70E0.

class_proposals.name: VehiclePhysicsBody
class_proposals.responsibility: Vehicle physics body state: speed-limit storage and clamping, velocity/angular-velocity integration (step 0.0125), attitude-angle computation, 3D position doubles, and conditional reset paths; updated by 0x0045A8E0.

class_proposals.name: HeightfieldProximityProcessor
class_proposals.responsibility: Processes a fixed-stride element table anchored at +0x134 with count at +0x130, driving VehicleProximity (0x004FB2E0) per element; invoked from heightfield collision processing.

class_proposals.name: GenericLinkedNode
class_proposals.responsibility: Reusable three-field linked node (data dword, next pointer, byte flag) initialized by 0x004BAC20; used as a node constructor across directory, collision, physics, AI, and network subsystems.

class_proposals.name: SessionScoringManager
class_proposals.responsibility: Racing/session scoring management struct: owns three allocations (+0x8C, +0x90, +0x94), a '1'-counted byte array, ~40 scalar/vector fields with -1.0/0/-1 defaults, and a trailing 0x28-byte 0xFF-sentinel block; reset by 0x004BB950.

interfaces.name: ISubControlBlockInitializer
interfaces.purpose: Uniform per-sub-control-block construction invoked by UIControlWindow::Initialize (0x004A70E0): each member constructs one block (sentinel seed, vtable header, state reset) via stride-based loops and batch iteration (0x00401000).

compatibility_contracts.name: UIWindowSubControlInit
compatibility_contracts.description: Constructing the profile/exists UI window must zero the leading callback/state fields (+0x0..+0x10), seed every sub-control block with sentinel defaults, assign vtable pointers from the fixed table 0x005ACB6C..0x005ACBFC, reset each block's state dword to 0 and target/sentinel to -1, zero the tail flags, and apply player-options defaults (0x004AA270).

compatibility_contracts.name: VehiclePhysicsBodySpeedLimit
compatibility_contracts.description: A speed-limit request must be stored at +0x24, clamped against the +0x1C/+0x20 bounds, and, when within bounds and integration enabled (+0xD0), integrated at step 0.0125 and emitted as 3D position (+0xD8/+0xE0/+0xE8) via 0x0054B4D0; out-of-range requests follow the clamp or reset path.

compatibility_contracts.name: SessionScoringStructReset
compatibility_contracts.description: Resetting the session/scoring struct must free the +0x8C, +0x90, and +0x94 allocations, count '1' entries of the +0x94 byte array into +0x98 before freeing, restore ~40 scalar fields (floats to -1.0, indexes to 0/-1), memset the trailing 0x28 bytes to 0xFF, and return -1.

subsystem.name: MathAndCollision
subsystem.responsibility: Stateless geometry/vector math primitives (ray-sphere intersection, 2D direction projection, SSE two-point interpolation), a collision-geometry container owning strut and struct arrays with nearest-neighbor queries and destructor teardown, and two standalone global-workspace sparse-matrix LDLT constraint solvers.

source_proposals.summary: The math_and_collision scope contains three groups. (1) CollisionPrimitives: stateless math helpers - a ray-sphere quadratic intersection test feeding the vehicle suspension force calculation (0x00401180), a 2D direction projection (0x00423AD0) used in AI/opponent proximity, and an SSE two-point linear interpolation (0x0051F6A0). (2) CollisionModel: a collision-geometry container owning a 316-byte-stride strut array (+0x134, count +0x130), a 28-byte-stride struct array (+0x154) and further buffers (+0x150/+0x158); it supports nearest-neighbor queries over linked nodes and struts (0x00403640), indexed struct copies (0x00403F70), and a destructor-style teardown (0x004045F0) freeing every owned allocation. (3) SparseConstraintSolver: two standalone block LDL^T factorization and substitution-solve kernels (0x0056FA96, 0x00575BBD) operating on global double constraint-matrix workspaces and row-pointer tables, returning 0. All owners are UNKNOWN at the function-IR level; the classes above are DERIVED/GUESS proposals.

function_roles.role: Ray-sphere quadratic intersection test on six double inputs; returns 1/sqrt(p) penetration-length proxy or 0.0 on any miss; used by the vehicle suspension force calculation

Nearest-neighbor spatial query over linked collision nodes (next at +0x110/+0x10C) and the 316-byte-stride strut array (this+0x134, count this+0x130), gated by a signed plane-distance probe; returns closest qualifying node or plane-verified candidate
Read getter: copies two 12-byte (3-dword) blocks out of element a2 of the 28-byte-stride struct array at this+0x154 into a3/a4 and returns a4; called from AI-driver and proximity paths

Destructor-style teardown: frees the three owned buffers (+0x150/+0x154/+0x158), nulls them and writes -1.0f at +0x148, walks the 316-byte-stride element array (+0x134, count from length prefix at base-4) calling per-element release, frees the array allocation, resets +0x130/+0x134/+0x138, returns prior array base; called from Game_Post
2D scalar projection of vector a2 onto vector a1 (components x at +0x0, z at +0x8): dot(a1,a2)/dot(a1,a1), returning 0.0 for a zero-length a1; AI/opponent proximity context
SSE two-point linear interpolation helper: a1 = a2 + (a3-a2)*a5 + (a4-a2)*a6 on packed two-point vectors (high halves only), storing result into a1 and returning a1

Block LDL^T factorization of a sparse dynamics constraint matrix plus substitution solve, carried out entirely on global double workspaces (factor blocks 0x008CFBF0-0x008CFC28 area, diagonals/accumulators 0x008D3A28-0x008D3B60, row blocks via pointer tables 0x008D3988-0x008D3A24); no callees, returns 0

Block-structured LDL^T factorization (symmetric-indefinite Cholesky variant) of a global double constraint matrix 0x008D2120..0x008D3978 driven by row-pointer array 0x008D3B68..0x008D3BF0; reciprocal-diagonal pivots, L-column scaling, Schur rank-1 updates, RHS forward elimination and back-substitution writing the final solve entry to 0x008D3870; no parameters, returns 0

class_proposals.name: CollisionPrimitives
class_proposals.responsibility: Stateless geometric/vector math primitives: ray-sphere quadratic intersection (suspension contact), 2D direction projection, and SSE two-point linear interpolation. No instance fields, no callees; grouped by shape only (owner identity not proven by the packet).

class_proposals.name: CollisionModel
class_proposals.responsibility: Container object owning the collision geometry arrays: a 316-byte-stride element (strut) array at +0x134 with count at +0x130, a 28-byte-stride struct array at +0x154, and further owned buffers at +0x150/+0x158. Supports nearest-neighbor queries over linked nodes and struts, indexed struct reads, and a destructor-style teardown freeing every owned allocation. Name is descriptive; packet reports owner UNKNOWN.

class_proposals.name: SparseConstraintSolver
class_proposals.responsibility: Standalone numeric kernel: block LDL^T factorization and substitution solve of sparse dynamics constraint matrices stored in global double workspaces (0x008CFBF0..0x008D3B60 and 0x008D2120..0x008D3978) indexed by global row-pointer arrays. No parameters, no callees, returns 0. Two independent functions grouped by shared algorithm and overlapping global workspace region.

compatibility_contracts.name: SuspensionRaySphereContact
compatibility_contracts.description: Ray-sphere quadratic intersection used by the vehicle suspension force calculation: takes six doubles, returns 0.0 on any miss and 1/sqrt(p) as a penetration-length proxy on hit. Must remain a pure scalar float-returning function with no side effects or callees.

compatibility_contracts.name: CollisionModelOwnedBufferLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: The collision container owns pointer buffers at +0x150/+0x154/+0x158 and a 316-byte-stride element array at +0x134 (count +0x130) whose allocation is length-prefixed 4 bytes before the base. Teardown frees each non-null buffer via FreeWrapper_7bcf, runs per-element release (0x004B0170) over the element array, frees the array allocation, nulls the pointers, writes -1.0f at +0x148, clears +0x130/+0x134/+0x138, and returns the prior array base.

compatibility_contracts.name: NearestNeighborQueryResult
compatibility_contracts.description: Nearest-neighbor query walks linked collision nodes (next pointers at +0x110/+0x10C) and the strut array (316-byte stride, entries with type field at +0x12C <= 1 distance-tested), using a signed plane-distance probe (0x004FB6D0). Returns a node pointer, preferring the plane-verified candidate when its final signed distance is non-negative.

compatibility_contracts.name: SparseConstraintSolverWorkspace
compatibility_contracts.description: Two standalone LDLT solvers factor global double constraint-matrix workspaces (0x008CFBF0..0x008D3B60 and 0x008D2120..0x008D3978) indexed by global row-pointer arrays (0x008D3988..0x008D3A24 and 0x008D3B68..0x008D3BF0); both take no parameters and return 0. A replacement must keep these global buffers and pointer tables byte-compatible.

CollisionModel name is descriptive; the packet reports owner identity UNKNOWN. Field +0x138 is only observed being reset to 0 in teardown; its live role is unknown.

The two solver functions share overlapping global workspace regions (0x008D3A28..0x008D3B60 is touched by both) but operate on disjoint matrix buffers; whether they are two phases of one solver, two solver instances, or two independent kernels is not provable from the packet.

subsystem.name: UiPlatformAndOptions
subsystem.responsibility: Options/settings UI platform: builds and owns the player options tree (named category groups of typed 9-dword entries, string-field registrations, default control-action key bindings, root enable flag life-cycle), destroys UI objects through a vtable-installing base-chain destructor, sets device state 18 via a vtable+252 dispatch, and suspends an AI thread under mutex.

source_proposals.summary: This scope covers the options/settings UI platform. The dominant function, PlayerOptions::initializer (0x004AA270), builds the full options tree: it creates category groups (Scene, Driver, DrivingAids, RaceConditions, SoundOptions, GraphicOptions, GameOptions, MultiplayerOptions, Options, Controls), registers string fields, fills every option entry as a 9-dword (36-byte) group via a family of setter helpers, formats indexed names in 7-entry loops, runs controller (2x8) and FFB-joystick (2x8) axis loops, and binds all control actions to default key codes. A small UI-object destructor (0x00494470) installs vtable 0x005AC830, chains the base destructor and optionally frees the object. Two unrelated helpers travel in the same scope: a device state-18 setter (0x00554560) that dispatches through vtable+252 on global 0x008B89A0, and a mutex-guarded thread suspend (0x005855E0) flagged by the packet as part of the ai subsystem. Owners of the destructor, the device setter and the thread suspend are UNKNOWN; only the options-tree owner (PlayerOptions) is DERIVED.

function_roles.role: UI object destructor with optional self-free: installs vtable 0x005AC830 at this+0x0, chains the base UI destructor, and when the flag argument has bit 0 set frees the object allocation; returns this.

Builds and initializes the player options/settings tree: creates the category groups (Scene, Driver, DrivingAids, RaceConditions, SoundOptions, GraphicOptions, GameOptions, MultiplayerOptions, Options, Controls), registers string fields, fills every option entry as a 9-dword (36-byte) group, formats indexed names in 7-entry loops, runs controller/FFB axis loops, and binds all control actions to default key codes.

State-18 conditional setter on a game device object: guards redundant sets (a2 == -1 or a2 == this[13]), dispatches vtable+252 on global 0x008B89A0 for a2 0/1 (value 1 or 2 depending on 0x008B8C48 bit 0), records the last applied a2 at this+0x34.
Mutex-guarded thread suspension with a 50-attempt retry loop and suspend-flag bookkeeping (fields this+0x4 thread handle, this+0x20 mutex, this+0x24 timeout, this+0x1C suspend flag).

class_proposals.name: PlayerOptions
class_proposals.responsibility: Owns and initializes the player options / settings tree: named category groups of 9-dword option entries, string-field registrations, control-action default key bindings, and the root enable flag life-cycle. Built by 0x004AA270 under UIControlWindowInitialization (0x004A70E0).

FlagSetterWithGlobalUpdate sets root enable flag to 1
FlagSetterWithGlobalUpdate clears root enable flag to 0, then EmptyStub finalizer

interfaces.name: SettingsGroupBuilder
interfaces.purpose: Builds the named category path (e.g. Scene, Driver, SoundOptions) under which option entries are registered.

interfaces.name: StringFieldRegistrar
interfaces.purpose: Registers a string-valued field into the current settings group (used for scene file, profile vehicle, telemetry exe/file, GDB filename, player livery).

compatibility_contracts.name: UIObjectLifetime
compatibility_contracts.description: UI object destruction must install vtable 0x005AC830 at this+0x0, chain to the base UI destructor (0x00485EB0), and when the flag argument has bit 0 set free the object allocation via FreeWrapper_7bcf; the call still returns this.

compatibility_contracts.name: DeviceState18Set
compatibility_contracts.description: Setting device state 18 for a2 0/1 must dispatch through vtable+252 on the object at global 0x008B89A0 (state 18, value 0 / 1-or-2 depending on bit 0 of global byte 0x008B8C48), skip when a2 == -1 or equals the last applied value, and record the last applied value at this+0x34.

compatibility_contracts.name: PlayerOptionsTreeLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: The options/settings tree is populated as named category groups (Scene, Driver, DrivingAids, RaceConditions, SoundOptions, GraphicOptions, GameOptions, MultiplayerOptions, Options, Controls); each option entry is a 9-dword (36-byte) group holding a label, value/min/max/selector dwords and a description string; indexed lists use 7-entry loops with per-index formatted names; all control actions are bound to default key codes; the root enable flag is set to 1 at start and cleared to 0 at end.

subsystem.name: VehicleAIPitControl
subsystem.responsibility: Per-frame AI driver control and pit-stop decision logic for race vehicles: AI tick orchestration (pre-race init vs racing path), waypoint/racing-line following, steering-target computation and lane scoring, driver-status state machine, AI ability drift, and tire-compound pit-stop scheduling with retirement.

source_proposals.summary: The vehicle AI subsystem drives one race vehicle per frame. AIMainUpdate (0x00424E70) is the tick orchestrator: it gates on aiEnableFlag, runs a pre-race/formation init branch and a racing branch, and commits control outputs into the vehicle input fields (0x3580/0x3584/0x357C). AIDriverStructInit (0x00424790) reinitialises the per-vehicle AI field block. The racing path delegates to AIWaypointSteeringUpdate (0x00426430), AIRacingLine (0x00425920), computeSteeringTarget (0x004270A0) and a driverStatus state machine (0..7) that dispatches SteeringAngleController (0x00425670) and related sub-functions. updateAIAbility (0x00429470) drifts the driver ability value and drives pit-stop decisions; PitStopDecisionTireCompound (0x0042A3D0) schedules tire compounds and can retire the vehicle. AISteeringRacingLineCorrection (0x0042B0E0) adjusts steering against the racing line. Two UNKNOWN-owner dispatch helpers (0x00409F40, 0x0040B360) perform chained vtable dispatch.

function_roles.role: Chained vtable dispatch helper: calls slot vtable+0x18 on this, then slot +0x1C on the non-null result and returns the second result, else the first.
Chained virtual dispatch helper: calls slot vtable+24 on this, then slot +28 on the non-null result, else returns the first result.

Per-frame AI driver subsystem reinitialization: clears AI state flags/timers/counters, seeds waypoint sentinels, resets pace/grip/pit/speed defaults, optionally reloads waypoint data and command-queue buffers.

Per-frame AI tick orchestrator: entry gate on AIEnableFlag, pre-race/formation init path, and racing path (heading vectors, driveability gate, lap-push, AIAbility refresh, pit entry/exit transitions, driverStatus 0..7 dispatch).
AI steering-angle and driver-status controller: follow-target steering (state 6) vs direction-vector steering, steering-error accumulator, position-snapshot timer toggling states 6/0.

AI racing-line and speed-profile update: waypoint chain resolution, lead-car aero drag, tire-force energy-decay speed profile, overtaking threat scoring, throttle/brake targets and overtaking-window flag.

AI waypoint-following and steering update: speed magnitude, waypoint re-query on drift, 20-node look-ahead chain rebuild, pit-lane entry command dispatch, tire-force grip solve, 0..3 speed zone, boundary-clamped steering targets.
AI steering-target computation: 5-lane boundary scan, centre steering, lane scoring via spatial queries, overtaking state transitions and session-time steering overrides.

Per-frame AI ability/driver tick: engagement-mode selection, difficulty scaling, per-frame ability drift and probability override, steering-target recompute, pit-stop decision logic (pit exit, tire-compound duration, fuel-weight pit exit).
Per-frame AI pit-stop logic: tire-compound selection vs lap count and session state, wing-repair lap records re-arm, vehicle retirement on blocking condition.

subsystem.name: VehiclePhysics
subsystem.responsibility: Per-frame vehicle physics: suspension strut contact solving and swept collision detection, tire/grip force propagation with distance falloff, per-wheel spring/damper forces, tire-model session initialization, steering geometry, and the vehicle-level control and physics timestep integration.

source_proposals.summary: Reconstructed proposal for the vehicle_physics subsystem from ten validated function IR entries: a suspension-strut solver chain (VehicleSuspensionForceCalculation -> SweptSuspensionCollisionDetection -> PhysicsNodePropagationWithDistanceFalloff) owned by a VehiclePhysicsNode class, a per-wheel spring/damper force kernel (WheelSpringDamperForceAndSteering), a tire-model initializer (TireModelFullInitialize, owner VehicleTireModel), a vehicle control/steering layer (VehicleMainPhysicsUpdate, SteeringGeometryUpdate), a physics timestep and wheel-dynamics state (VehiclePhysicsTimeStep, WheelStateReset) and a physics state buffer clearer (PhysicsBufferClear). Class membership, field names and contracts are DERIVED/GUESS proposals; common ownership of the control-state this object is unproven and recorded in unresolved.

function_roles.role: Per-strut suspension contact solver: iterates the suspension strut array (this+0x134, stride 316, count this+0x130), queries the spatial grid for the node/feature contact pair, builds a contact frame, applies gravity compensation, runs ray-sphere intersection tests and writes penetration depth and contact force per strut.

Swept-strut contact solver: Euler-advances each strut position over the strut array, sweeps the travel axis over a small window calling the suspension and tire force solvers at every sample, and commits the sample position that maximizes contact force.

Per-frame force propagation: runs the swept suspension solver then the full-grid suspension solver, propagates tire and grip forces along each strut's linked node chain with distance falloff into strut+136/+140, computes the maximum propagated force at this+0x148, then applies a grip-multiplier pass (sub_4FB260) and a per-strut finalization pass (sub_4FAF60).
Clears the 40-dword physics state buffer (dwords 0..38) and, if the pointer at +0x9C is non-null, frees it through FreeWrapper_7bcf and nulls the slot; returns the previous buffer pointer.

Full per-wheel tire physics initialization: builds each wheel's compliance matrix and stiffness/damper/thermal state, looks up and applies the tire brand and compound, computes front/rear suspension compliance and attach-point geometry, copies the session setup envelope, allocates and pre-fills the interpolated tire-curve table, seeds wear/thermal session tables, pulls session-state values and finishes by zeroing run state and setting init markers (this+0x30=-2, this+0x34=3).

Per-wheel steering geometry update: scales steering input to radians, adds deterministic trig-table noise, accumulates per-wheel steering angles with clamping, frees the physics sub-object, then transforms the wheel contact geometry through the coordinate frames of the matching contact bodies and sets a secondary-state steering flag on threshold.

Main per-frame vehicle control tick: snapshots raw controller bytes, maps inputs into steering/throttle/brake commands, runs steering damping, heading-limit clamps, tire-force projection against the track center line, collision/obstacle avoidance, lap/position state transitions, control-mode speed logic, per-wheel torque/brake distribution and final gearbox dispatch.

Per-frame physics timestep: computes frame delta time, decodes the packed input packet via the bitfield/short-vector helper family, transforms state into the vehicle struct, runs per-wheel suspension updates, dispatches mode-specific state machines (mode 2 = full setup copy + subsystem loop; mode 3 = vibration + subsystem loop) and derives braking/audio/bit flags.

Per-frame spring/damper force and steering computation for one wheel: builds an orthonormal frame from the suspension axis (near-vertical fast path and 2D fallback), computes contact-frame forces, updates spring stiffness and force magnitude, tracks contact-patch displacement, clamps forces to the friction/grip circle and writes the force components back along the wheel local axes.

Per-frame reset of the vehicle wheel-dynamics state: first-frame WheelDynamicsInit guard, frees the heap object at this+0x39A4, zeroes the per-frame physics accumulator block, resets four per-wheel dynamics records (62 dwords each, identity 1.0 entries) and writes the frame sentinel this+0x39F4 = -2.

transitions: read global dword_7CEA5C: 0 selects disable, 1..3 select scaling
when session type dword_7C56A4 == 7, this+0x1DB4 is additionally divided by flt_8ACF9C

subsystem.name: VehiclePhysics
subsystem.responsibility: Per-frame vehicle wheel/suspension/tire force simulation (contact-patch adjustment, weight distribution, per-wheel suspension and tire state, anti-roll-bar and drivetrain parameters, 13-point contact transform, force-model summation, wheel output publish) plus the per-vehicle tire model configuration data that the simulation consumes.

source_proposals.summary: Three functions. UpdateSuspensionAndWheelPhysics (0x004E5F60) is the per-frame vehicle physics update owned by the vehicle object (this): it copies and adjusts the four wheel contact-patch positions, recomputes weight distribution from the car-setup argument a2, rebuilds per-wheel suspension/tire state (temperatures, loads, spring/damper split), computes anti-roll-bar mixing and drivetrain/mass parameters, runs a 13-point contact-position transform (bitmask-driven tweaks, bounding-radius tracking), evaluates six polynomial/tire-force helper models, sums the force vector, applies session (a3) offsets to tracked contact points, fills a 13-point particle buffer, writes wheel output positions, and returns an advanced pointer into the session block. SetWheelForceParameters (0x004F1BA0) is a conditional wheel force/torque setter on the same vehicle object: when the physics-mode flag at +0x32BC is set it stores four per-wheel parameters into the per-wheel blocks (stride 248, force field at block offset 0x24), otherwise it applies them directly to a rigid body via an inertia-tensor helper; called from pit-stop progress (0x004A68B0). TireModelDataInit (0x004F34E0) is a bulk constructor for a distinct per-vehicle tire model data object (ABI lead Tire_Model_Data_Init, LEGACY): handle sentinels (0 and -1), compound count 15, friction/camber/slip coefficient seeding, multiple zero-init sub-structures and zero runs, four 66-dword physics-default sub-structs, and a config-path string copy through StringCopyWithBufferRealloc on global 0x005EA438.

function_roles.role: Per-frame vehicle physics update: contact-patch position copy/adjust/bias, weight-distribution recompute, per-wheel suspension/tire state rebuild, anti-roll-bar and drivetrain/mass parameter computation, 13-point contact-position transform with bitmask tweaks and bounding-radius tracking, force-model summation and smoothing, session-offset application to tracked contact points, particle buffer fill, wheel output publish, session-block pointer advance.

Conditional wheel force/torque parameter setter: when the physics-mode flag at +0x32BC is non-zero stores four per-wheel parameters into the wheel-force fields (per-wheel blocks at +0x3664/+0x375C/+0x3854/+0x394C, stride 248); otherwise applies them directly as force/torque to a rigid body via the inertia-tensor helper using global dbl_7C7428. Used during pit-stop wheel operations (caller 0x004A68B0).

Bulk constructor/initializer for the per-vehicle tire model data object: handle sentinels (primary 0, others -1) and compound count, friction/camber/slip coefficient seeding, physics-constant and per-compound coefficient seeding, multiple zero-init sub-structures and zero runs, four 66-dword physics-default sub-structs in a fixed loop, sub-constructor call, and config-path string copy through StringCopyWithBufferRealloc on global 0x005EA438. ABI lead name Tire_Model_Data_Init (LEGACY).

class_proposals.name: Vehicle
class_proposals.responsibility: Per-vehicle runtime state consumed and produced by the per-frame physics update and the pit-stop wheel-force setter: wheel contact geometry, weight distribution, per-wheel suspension/tire state blocks (stride 248), drivetrain, engine, aero, force accumulators, 13-point contact output, particle/effect state, tracked contact points, and the published body position. The physics-mode flag at +0x32BC gates both functions.

class_proposals.name: TireModelData
class_proposals.responsibility: Per-vehicle tire model configuration data constructed once (ABI lead Tire_Model_Data_Init, LEGACY): compound handle slots with 0/-1 sentinels, compound count 15, friction/camber/slip coefficients, physics and per-compound coefficient tables, zero-initialized runtime accumulator runs, four 66-dword physics-default sub-structs, and the tire config path loaded through StringCopyWithBufferRealloc from global 0x005EA438.

interfaces.name: TireCompoundResolution
interfaces.purpose: Resolve the tire brand (TireBrandLookup on global table 0x008AD254 with the session compound id a3+136) and then the compound index (CompoundIndexLookup on the brand pointer and the compound selection) into the two base pointers into the compound data used by the wheel force evaluation.

interfaces.name: SuspensionForceEvaluation
interfaces.purpose: Per-wheel suspension and tire force helper models: suspension force split (VehicleSuspensionForceHelper), quadratic/cubic polynomial evaluators, tire force/torque computation, quadratic force model, linear vehicle parameter evaluation, and quadratic force/torque curve evaluation, whose outputs feed the force summation.

interfaces.name: WheelStateInitialization
interfaces.purpose: Initialize the per-wheel suspension/tire state from the wheel index, contact offset pointer, and steering-direction magnitudes (WheelSuspensionTireStateInit).

interfaces.name: RuntimeParameterHelpers
interfaces.purpose: Auxiliary runtime value generators used by the per-frame update: parameterized torque-curve interpolation, random offset and bias value computation, arithmetic comparison/validation, and float-to-int conversion and allocation count arithmetic.

interfaces.name: AllocationAndSystemServices
interfaces.purpose: Memory allocation and system helper services: operator-new wrapper and float-to-int conversion, LCG random seeding, triple-field position query, vertex/particle buffer allocation, direction-vector projection, and config-path string copy with reallocation.

interfaces.name: SimulationServices
interfaces.purpose: Simulation-level services invoked from the per-frame update and the tire model data constructor: session-state indexed lookup, pit-part state copy, engine wear/failure simulation, 3x3 matrix transform with translation, loop-with-conditional-subcall, and the zero-init/sub-constructor helpers.

subsystem.name: VehiclePhysics
subsystem.responsibility: Vehicle configuration loading (.SVM/.HDV line parsing into an internal setup struct plus a normalized output vehicle-state struct) and physics dynamics-matrix identity initialization.

source_proposals.summary: Two functions. ParseSvmHdvVehicleConfigFile (0x004F4270) is a line-by-line .SVM/.HDV parser owned by TheSvmHdvVehicleFileParser (DERIVED from the legacy ABI lead): it opens the file in binary-read mode, validates the format on a first pass, dispatches each named section (General, FrontWing, LeftFender, RightFender, RearWing, BodyAero, Diffuser, Suspension, Controls, Engine, Driveline, per-wheel corners, Basic) to a section reader, resolves secondary files (damage model, engine, gear file, physical model, tire compound) relative to the config path, and normalizes range/setting pairs into the output vehicle state. InitPhysicsTransformIdentity (0x00578F76) is a selector dispatch (0..33) that initializes one row of a large double-precision physics dynamics matrix block (0x008D2120..0x008D3978) to an identity row (diagonal 1.0, off-diagonals 0.0), returning the selector argument.

function_roles.role: Line-by-line parser and section dispatcher for .SVM/.HDV vehicle configuration files; validates format, parses named sections, resolves secondary files, and normalizes range/setting pairs into the output vehicle-state struct.
Initialize one row of the double-precision physics dynamics matrix to an identity row; dispatch on selector argument a1 (0..33) via the jump table at 0x00579C47 and return the selector.

class_proposals.name: TheSvmHdvVehicleFileParser
class_proposals.responsibility: Parse .SVM/.HDV vehicle configuration files into an internal setup struct (this) and produce a normalized output vehicle-state struct (a3); dispatch named sections to section readers and resolve secondary files relative to the config path.

interfaces.name: ConfigTokenReader
interfaces.purpose: Low-level token/line readers and section-header matcher used by the SVM/HDV parser to decode individual config lines into typed values and to route lines to section readers.

compatibility_contracts.name: SvmHdvConfigFileFormat
compatibility_contracts.description: Line-based '='-delimited configuration files with named sections (General, FrontWing, LeftFender, RightFender, RearWing, BodyAero, Diffuser, Suspension, Controls, Engine, Driveline, Frontleft/Frontright/Rearleft/Rearright, Basic). Recognized header keywords include Setting/Notes/Downforce/Balance/Ride/Gearing/Custom/Symmetric. In non-server sessions a file with no recognized header is rejected as an illegal .SVM file. A replacement executable must preserve '=' delimiter handling, section dispatch, and the rejection path.

compatibility_contracts.name: PhysicsMatrixRowIdentity
compatibility_contracts.description: 0x00578F76 must set exactly one row of the double-precision dynamics matrix to an identity row (diagonal element 1.0, all other stored elements of that row 0.0), selected by argument 0..33, and return the selector argument unchanged on every path.
